cocktails.name: San Fermo Negroni

ingredients.name: Gin
ingredients.description: Juniper-forward base spirit; gives the Negroni its botanical backbone.

ingredients.name: Campari
ingredients.description: The iconic Italian bitter aperitivo — bright red, orange-and-rhubarb bitter, the soul of a Negroni.

ingredients.name: Amaricano Bianco
ingredients.description: A clear American-made bitter aperitivo (Fast Penny, Seattle); softer and more floral than Campari, it lightens the build.

ingredients.name: Yzaguirre barrel-aged sweet vermouth
ingredients.description: A Spanish (Catalan) sweet vermouth rested in barrel — richer, rounder, and spicier than standard rosso, adding depth and a long finish.

ingredients.name: Rose tincture
ingredients.description: A house infusion of rose; a whisper of floral aromatics lifts the nose.

ingredients.name: Grapefruit expression
ingredients.description: Oils squeezed from a grapefruit peel over the surface — citrus aromatics to greet the first sip.

cocktails.name: Imaginary Friend
cocktails.build: mezcal, spiced red wine and balsamic agrodolce, amaro lucano, lime, veso fig leaf vermouth, black lemon bitters

ingredients.name: Mezcal
ingredients.description: A Mexican spirit distilled from roasted agave. Unlike tequila, the agave piñas are pit-roasted over hot rocks before fermentation, giving mezcal its signature smokiness. Earthy, complex, and layered — vegetal sweetness under the smoke, with a long finish. The base of the whole cocktail.

ingredients.description: A fig-leaf vermouth from Veso.

ingredients.name: Black lemon bitters

nonAlcoholic.name: House Mocktail
nonAlcoholic.note: Rotates with the season and the walk-in. Ask your bar lead for tonight's build before service so you can speak to it.

nonAlcoholic.name: Pathfinder N/A Negroni
nonAlcoholic.note: Seattle-born zero-proof spirit: fermented hemp, distilled in copper pots, layered with wormwood, angelica, sage, ginger, and Douglas fir. Reads like an amaro — earthy, bittersweet, crisp — stirred here into a Negroni-style build. No cannabinoids, nothing psychoactive. First poured at Life on Mars in 2021.

nonAlcoholic.name: Aplos Ginger and Red Shiso "Sour"
nonAlcoholic.note: Zero-proof sour built on Aplos, a hemp-infused alcohol-free spirit, shaken with a red shiso ginger syrup (made from Katie's own red shiso) over lemon. Tart and herbaceous, with a gingery bite and a garden edge from the shiso.

nonAlcoholic.name: Noughty N/A Sparkling Chardonnay
nonAlcoholic.note: Thomson & Scott's alcohol-free sparkling: 100% organic Spanish chardonnay, dealcoholized under vacuum so the aromatics survive, then lightly carbonated. Crisp green apple, a touch of sweetness, real acidity. 0.0%, organic, vegan.

beer.name: Menabrea Lager
beer.note: Birra Menabrea 1846 — a family-run lager from Biella in the Piedmont Alps, brewed with pure mountain water since 1846. Crisp and clean with a gentle floral aroma and a delicate bitter finish. An award-winning Italian classic.

beer.name: Fremont Brewing Lush IPA
beer.note: From Fremont Brewing, a few neighborhoods over — family-owned since 2009. Their year-round juicy IPA: Citra and Mosaic hops, tropical and citrus up front, smooth finish. 7%, drinks easier than it is.

beer.name: Athletic Brewing "Upside Dawn" Non-Alcoholic
beer.note: Athletic Brewing's non-alcoholic golden ale, under 0.5% ABV.

amaroFlights.name: It's Not What You'd Expect!

pours.name: Amaro Brucato "Fields"
pours.note: Brucato's fourth amaro, built from farm-field ingredients: artichoke leaf, beet root, rhubarb root and toasted dandelion, with fenugreek, dill and coriander. Macerated in California grape brandy and rested on toasted oak. Savory and herbal over caramel, softly bitter.

pours.name: Borsci San Marzano
pours.note: Elisir Borsci San Marzano, a recipe dating to 1840 and Giuseppe Borsci, now made by Distilleria Caffo. Melissa, wormwood, clove and saffron. Sweet and dark up front, then coffee, chocolate and orange, with a velvety bitter finish. Traditionally poured over ice cream or into coffee.

pours.name: Faccia Brutto Fernet
pours.note: Brooklyn-made fernet in the old Italian style — bracing, minty, properly bitter. The producer's name means 'ugly face,' which is roughly what the first sip makes.

amaroFlights.desc: Three amari that wrong-foot you. A California amaro built on artichoke and beet, a Puglian elixir from 1840 that tastes like coffee and chocolate, and a fernet from Brooklyn, not Milan. For the guest who's sure they know amaro.

amaroFlights.name: Out of the Woods

pours.name: Amaro Braulio
pours.note: The alpine classic, made in Bormio high in the Italian Alps since 1875 — juniper, gentian, wormwood, and yarrow, rested in oak. Tastes like pine air after snow.

pours.name: Amaro Amorino Reserva
pours.note: Letterpress Distilling, Seattle. Seville orange peel, baking spice, and florals, with the reserve bottling rested in used whiskey barrels at a fuller proof. Named for the founder's Abruzzo-born grandfather.

pours.name: Brucato Amaro Woodlands
pours.note: San Francisco amaro from California botanicals — elderberry, cocoa nib, black fig, and citrus. Dark, woodsy, gently sweet.

amaroFlights.desc: A walk through three forests: the Italian Alps, a Seattle barrel room, and California woodland. Piney, dark, resinous — the deep end of the genre.

amaroFlights.name: The Hill I Die On

pours.name: Brucato Amaro "Chaparral"
pours.note: Brucato's ode to California's chaparral scrubland — yerba santa, bay laurel, spearmint, cardamom. Green and herbal, pointed in the direction of Chartreuse.

pours.name: Amaro Foro
pours.note: From Piedmont, formulated by a former pharmacist — 25 botanicals over a citrus-peel core, angelica to chamomile. Dark, nutty, bittersweet.

pours.name: California Fernet
pours.note: A California take on the most divisive amaro — long botanical maceration, mint-forward and brighter than its Milanese ancestors, bottled at a full 40%.

amaroFlights.desc: Hillside botany with strong opinions — California chaparral scrub, a Piedmontese pharmacist's 25-botanical formula, and a fernet that picks a fight. Order it if you have convictions.

afterDinner.name: Espresso Martini
afterDinner.note: Vodka, espresso, coffee liqueur — cold, rich, caffeinated closer.

afterDinner.name: House Limoncello
afterDinner.note: House-made lemon liqueur; bright, sweet, clean finish. Made in-house.

afterDinner.name: Scuppoz Amaretto
afterDinner.note: Toasted almond and apricot kernel amaretto from Abruzzo, Italy; marzipan sweetness, nutty depth.

afterDinner.name: Scuppoz Amaro
afterDinner.note: Abruzzo, Italy (Scuppoz); artisanal mountain-herb amaro, made without added colorants.

afterDinner.name: Sambuca
afterDinner.note: Italian anise liqueur; sweet, licorice-forward, traditionally served with three coffee beans.

afterDinner.name: Dow's Tawny Porto 20 yr
afterDinner.note: Aged 20 years in cask; Douro Valley, Portugal. Nutty, dried fig, candied orange, warm spice.

afterDinner.name: Dow's Fine White Port
afterDinner.note: Fresh, golden white port; Douro Valley, Portugal. Crisp pear and citrus, nutty finish, slightly off-dry.

afterDinner.name: Mancino Edizione Sakura Vermouth
afterDinner.note: Limited-edition Torino-style vermouth; Kyoto cherry blossoms and Italian viola flowers, pale pink, delicately floral.

afterDinner.name: Lustau Oloroso Sherry
afterDinner.note: Fully oxidized dry sherry from Jerez, Spain. Dark, full-bodied; caramel, walnut, dried fruit, warm spice.

afterDinner.name: Lustau Pedro-Ximenez Sherry
afterDinner.note: Lusciously sweet sherry from Jerez, Spain. Sun-dried PX grapes; raisins, molasses, dark fig, velvety texture.

afterDinner.name: Amaricano Bianco
afterDinner.note: Seattle-made (Fast Penny Spirits); citrus-forward American bitter aperitivo. Candied lemon, saffron, apricot, chamomile.

afterDinner.name: Averna
afterDinner.note: Sicily, Italy (since 1868); bittersweet and caramel-rich, with orange peel and licorice. Smooth, approachable, a good first amaro.

afterDinner.name: Scarlet Orange Amaro
afterDinner.note: Japanese craft amaro by Iseya Distillery, Kanagawa. Blood orange-forward; bright citrus, lemon balm, gentle ginger heat.

afterDinner.name: Scarlet Fernet Amaro
afterDinner.note: Japanese craft fernet by Iseya Distillery; 30+ botanicals including mint, galangal, and palo santo. Botanical and layered, surprisingly smooth.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Foro Originale
afterDinner.note: Piedmontese amaro; 25 botanicals including gentian and angelica. Bittersweet citrus, dried herbs, clean bitter finish.

afterDinner.name: Faccia Brutto Fernet Pianta
afterDinner.note: Brooklyn-made (Faccia Brutto Spirits); 27 botanicals, mint-forward with citrus peel and licorice. More approachable than traditional fernet.

afterDinner.name: Faccia Brutto Amaro Gorini
afterDinner.note: Brooklyn-made (Faccia Brutto Spirits); barrel-aged in Solera style. Orange peel, chestnut honey, warm cinnamon and star anise.

afterDinner.name: Fernet Dogma
afterDinner.note: Chicago-made (CH Distillery); fernet with Dark Matter coffee and chamomile, finished in bourbon barrels. Coffee, spearmint, slight bitterness.

afterDinner.name: Fernet Francisco Rye Cask
afterDinner.note: San Francisco-made; 12 Bay Area botanicals finished in Willett rye casks. Herbal bitterness softened by vanilla, oak, and toasted rye spice.

afterDinner.name: Geijer California Fernet
afterDinner.note: San Francisco-made (Geijer Spirits); 21 botanicals, corn-base. Minty, bitter, grassier and drier than traditional fernet.

afterDinner.name: Amaro "Vino" Pasubio
afterDinner.note: Wine-based alpine amaro from Trentino by Cappelletti; mugo pine, blueberry, and smoky alpine herbs on a red wine base. Rare style.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Ciociaro
afterDinner.note: Lazio, Italy (Paolucci, since 1873); bitter orange backbone with chamomile, anise, and cinnamon. Bittersweet, approachable, lingers with chocolate and spice.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Sfumato
afterDinner.note: Trentino, Italy (Cappelletti); smoked Chinese rhubarb — the smoke is real. Deep, dark, earthy, bittersweet with an alpine herbal finish.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Montenegro
afterDinner.note: Bologna, Italy; 40 botanicals. Medium bitter, notably aromatic — orange peel, vanilla, coriander, rose petal. The gateway amaro for newcomers.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Meletti
afterDinner.note: Marche, Italy (since 1870); saffron, violet flower, anise, and orange peel. Caramelized orange and cola sweetness, floral, warm spice.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Del Etna
afterDinner.note: Sicily, Italy; 26+ herbs from the slopes of Mount Etna. Bitter citrus, licorice, cinnamon, and a distinct volcanic mineral character.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Amorino
afterDinner.note: Seattle-made (Letterpress Distilling); named for the founder's Italian grandfather. Seville orange peel, baking spice, vanilla, and floral notes. Light-to-medium bitter.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Amorino Reserva
afterDinner.note: Seattle-made (Letterpress Distilling); the reserve expression of Amorino. Same orange-spice-floral DNA, deeper and more layered from extended aging.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Nonino
afterDinner.note: Friuli, Italy (Nonino Distillery); grappa-based amaro aged in small oak barrels. Fruity and elegant — apricot, caramel, orange, gentian. One of the great Italian amari.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Cansiglio
afterDinner.note: Veneto, Italy; 18 herbs and berries from the ancient Cansiglio forest in the Dolomite foothills. Mint, pine, bitter orange, eucalyptus — fresh and invigorating.

afterDinner.name: Maraska Pelinkovac
afterDinner.note: Croatian wormwood liqueur; Dalmatia. Intensely bitter and herbal, dark fruit and dried spice, medicinal and unapologetic.

afterDinner.name: Cynar
afterDinner.note: Italy (Campari Group, since 1952); artichoke-led, 13 herbs. Vegetal, bittersweet — dark chocolate, walnut, caramel with a cola-like sweetness. Surprisingly approachable.

afterDinner.name: Braulio
afterDinner.note: Valtellina, Italy (since 1875 in Bormio, 4,000 ft altitude); juniper, wormwood, gentian, yarrow. Cooling piney character, mountain violet, mint, bittersweet alpine finish.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Brucato "Orchard"
afterDinner.note: San Francisco-made (Brucato Spirits); apricot, walnut, Meyer lemon, and cinnamon. Juicy, fruit-forward, warm baking spice. Think of it as a fruity California Campari.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Brucato "Chaparral"
afterDinner.note: San Francisco-made (Brucato Spirits); yerba santa, spearmint, cardamom. Herbal, minty, Chartreuse-like character. Coastal California hillsides in a glass.

afterDinner.name: Amaro Brucato "Fields"
afterDinner.note: San Francisco-made (Brucato Spirits); artichoke leaf, beet root, rhubarb root, fenugreek, dill. Savory and herbal over caramel, soft bitterness.

afterDinner.name: Nonino Grappa di Merlot
afterDinner.note: Friuli, Italy (Nonino Distillery); single-varietal pomace grappa from Merlot. Rose petal, ripe cherry, soft and velvety texture, delicate almond finish.

afterDinner.name: Nonino Grappa di Moscato
afterDinner.note: Friuli, Italy (Nonino Distillery); single-varietal pomace grappa from Moscato. Highly aromatic — rose, sage, vanilla, orange blossom. The most perfumed of the grappas.

afterDinner.name: Martel "Blue Swift" Cognac
afterDinner.note: Martell VSOP eaux-de-vie finished in Kentucky bourbon casks. Cognac fruit (fig, plum, pear) layered with vanilla, coconut, and toasted oak from the bourbon barrels.

afterDinner.name: Menorvall Calvados
afterDinner.note: Normandy, France; apple brandy, 40% ABV. Ripe pear aroma, baking spice, chamomile, sandalwood. Apple brandy that drinks closer to Armagnac than cider.

afterDinner.name: Compass Box Artist's Blend Scotch
afterDinner.note: Blended Scotch by Compass Box (UK); light and approachable. Butterscotch, toffee apple, vanilla, light fruit, creamy mouthfeel. Un-chill filtered, 43% ABV.

afterDinner.name: Glenlivet 12yr
afterDinner.note: Speyside single malt Scotch, Scotland. Fruit-forward and gentle — apple, pear, vanilla, light honey. No peat. The definitive entry-level Speyside.

afterDinner.name: Laphroaig 10yr
afterDinner.note: Islay single malt Scotch, Scotland. The most polarizing whisky on the list. Intense peat smoke, seaweed, iodine, and medicinal herbs over a surprising sweetness. Malted barley dried over Islay peat fires.

afterDinner.name: Lagavulin 16yr
afterDinner.note: Islay single malt Scotch, Scotland. Peat smoke with far more depth than Laphroaig — sherry richness, dark fruit, black tea, maritime brine, and a long smoky finish. The benchmark peated Scotch.

afterDinner.name: Weller 12yr
afterDinner.note: Kentucky straight bourbon, Buffalo Trace; wheated mash bill (wheat replaces rye). Exceptionally smooth — butterscotch, baked apple, cinnamon, vanilla, long oaky finish. Same wheat recipe as Pappy Van Winkle.
